summary:
Partula salifana was a small tree snail found nowhere else on Earth but the slopes of Mt. Alifan on Rota Island, Guam. Like its Partulid relatives, it likely lived quietly among the forest vegetation, part of an ancient and delicate web of island life. It was last seen alive in 1946, already a ghost of its former world.

Its disappearance was swift and human-caused. The intentional introduction of the predatory Rosy Wolfsnail in 1957, followed by the New Guinea Flatworm in 1978, devastated snail populations across Guam. Searches in the 1980s found only shells — silent evidence that Partula salifana had survived perhaps into the early 1980s before vanishing entirely, unnoticed, from a mountain that had been its only home.
